title: Motor Overload Tripped
shortDescription: Thermal overload has cut power to the motor.
fullDescription:
Whirlpool Gold Series disposals have a thermal overload that trips when the motor overheats or stalls. Allow 10 minutes cooling and press the red reset button on the underside.

Repeat trips indicate a hidden jam or worn motor.

fixSteps.title: Clear jam
fixSteps.instruction: Use Allen wrench in bottom port.

fixSteps.title: Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Press red reset button on underside.

whenToCallPro: If reset button does not stay in.

faq.a: Persistent jam or weak motor; inspect carefully.

title: Impellers Jammed
shortDescription: Motor hums but impellers do not turn.
fullDescription:
Jamming is the most common disposal issue. A hex key inserted in the bottom allows the user to manually rotate the shaft and free the impellers.

Always disconnect power before working on a disposal.

fixSteps.title: Rotate shaft
fixSteps.instruction: Hex key in bottom port, rotate both directions.

title: Water Leak Under Sink
shortDescription: Disposal leaking at one of several common points.
fullDescription:
Leaks commonly occur at the sink flange, dishwasher inlet, or discharge pipe. A cracked disposal body is rare but fatal to the unit.

Identify the source before acting.

fixSteps.title: Find source
fixSteps.instruction: Dry, then run water to locate leak point.

whenToCallPro: If body is cracked - replace unit.

title: Disposal Dead - No Response
shortDescription: No sound or motor activity when switched on.
fullDescription: No response usually means a tripped reset, breaker, or bad switch. Test each power source in order.
whenToCallPro: For hardwired units with no accessible plug.

faq.a: Code varies but GFCI is recommended for kitchen outlets.

title: Loud Grinding / Rattling
fullDescription:
A rattling disposal usually has something metallic or hard inside. Cut power and inspect with a flashlight.

A scraping sound can indicate worn impellers.
whenToCallPro: If noise continues with chamber empty.

title: Slow Drain
shortDescription: Sink backs up when disposal runs.
fullDescription:
A clog downstream of the disposal prevents drainage. Most often the p-trap is blocked.

Remove and clean the p-trap manually.

fixSteps.title: Clean p-trap
fixSteps.instruction: Bucket underneath, remove slip nuts, clean.

title: Motor Burned
fullDescription: Burning odors mean windings are overheating. Do not continue running; replace the disposal.

title: Dishwasher Drain Backup
shortDescription: Water from dishwasher backs up in sink.
fullDescription:
New disposal installs require knockout plug removal to accept dishwasher drain water. A retained plug causes backup.

Remove plug via the inlet.
symptoms: Water in sink after dishwasher cycle

fixSteps.title: Remove knockout
fixSteps.instruction: Tap out plug with screwdriver and hammer.

whenToCallPro: If plumbing beyond disposal is blocked.

faq.a: Only when connected to a dishwasher.
